name: YHVH
overview: YHVH is the male, holy God whose holiness is emphasized by the triple declaration "Holy, Holy, Holy" as found in Isaiah 6:3. He is uniquely set apart, embodying divine perfection and sovereignty. No tribe or additional personal notes are recorded, underscoring His transcendence and singularity.
namesAndTitles: YHVH is known by many names and titles that reveal His divine nature and sovereign roles. Titles such as "G-d," meaning rulers or judges, "LORD G-d," and "G-d Almighty" emphasize His supreme authority and power. Names like "G-d Who Sees" and "Judge of all the earth" further illustrate His omniscience and righteous judgment as given by God Himself in various Old Testament passages.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records YHVH as the Creator of Adam and the master or lord over many key biblical figures including Abram, Moses, Caleb, David, Job, Isaiah, and others. He is explicitly noted as the killer of Er and Onan and the one who was born by Mary, reflecting His incarnation in Christ. Additionally, He serves as the rabbi to Simon and king to the captain of the host of the LORD, highlighting His authoritative relationships throughout biblical history.
scriptureSignificance: YHVH is central to the biblical narrative as the holy and sovereign God who creates, judges, and governs all creation. His many names and titles reflect His multifaceted character as creator, redeemer, and ruler. His direct involvement with key biblical figures demonstrates His active presence and authority in human history. Ultimately, YHVH's holiness and lordship point forward to the fullness of revelation in Jesus Christ, the incarnate God born of Mary.
